title: Ask HN: Anyone know someone at GitHub to help expedite a support request?
text: Background: I've been working with a new company to help deliver a project. I got set up with a Google account for them (so I have myname@example.com), and I created a new Github account to associate with that email, and connected everything together. For the first week everything was fine, I was fixing issues, putting up PRs, etc. One of the last PRs I was able to put up was a CI fix -- we had 10 CI checks that hadn't passed in months, and by fixing the underlying issue they started running. That ended up being an issue however -- they started running very long running tasks, and our Github Action minutes spiked up. Soon after, my account was suspended, with no email, no warning, nothing. The CTO who had Github org admin access could see that I had been suspended, and nothing else. Both he on behalf of the Github Enterprise organization and myself personally submitted a ticket up, and got no response so far. We waited over the weekend, and still didn't get a response. Since we had a deadline of before Thanksgiving, and we weren't hearing back anything from Github, my company spun me up a new Google account and Github account, just so I could start contributing. A few hours later, that account was banned as well. It's very frustrating -- and even our Enterprise organization seems to get no recourse. Is there any good solution here?

title: Ask HN: Can I map all the arguments in a topic to "approach the truth"?
text: Hi HN, I wanted to take a stance on these topics people have been arguing all around. There should be some sort of answer, right? I used to go to debates for that end. But I often only see the repetition of the same points, the hardest objection being dodged, etc. I tried AI as well, but it only returns surface level arguments likewise. Is there anyway to preserve debate's purpose in trying to see the deepest case, while getting over these “sophistry”? Could I map all the arguments in controversial topics (continuously allowing new inputs), and rephrase and put them in a clear sequence, so fallacies, detours, and claims already have well-established answers could be cleared out, leaving only the real tradeoff standing? I tried it: creating TruthTree (Truthtree.app). Anything it has missed, you can hit "Challenge this claim”, type your counter, and if it's spot on (through the AI, with a fallback checker), it will be on the tree. For example, for abortion, the map currently filters out this unanswered crux: "knowingly creating a life that depends on your body gives you a duty to continue the pregnancy."(https://truthtree.app/abortion/responsibility) Is that the answer to abortion? What’s the map missing? Please also let me know if this format works, and if there’s anything that could be changed to make things easier!

title: Show HN: Outloud Reader – photograph a page and listen to it phrase by phrase
text: Hi HN, I built Outloud Reader, an iOS and Android app that reads any page aloud. You take a photo of a page, open a PDF, or paste text, and it reads it aloud in a natural voice, highlighting each phrase as it is spoken. How the idea was born: My wife has been learning English for many years but she never gets real practice. One day she told me it would be great to have an app that could turn any photo of text into audio, so she could practice her listening while walking or driving. That's what inspired me to build Outloud Reader. Yes, I know there are many text-to-speech apps, but most of them just read the text or cost too much. What it does: - Every phrase lights up as it's spoken, so you can read along - 14 languages, with a woman's or a man's voice in most of them - If you're learning a language, it can translate the page into the language you're learning - If you have nothing to listen to, ask AI to write a short text at your level (A1–C2) and turn it into audio - The finished audio is stored on your phone, so it works offline - On iPhone and iPad your library syncs through iCloud, so you can start on your phone and keep listening on your tablet - No sign-up, no email, no ads How it works: The page goes to my server, an LLM recognizes the text and translates it if you ask, then it is voiced with a mix of open-source and cloud voices depending on the language. The phrase highlighting comes from aligning the audio with the text. The apps are native on both platforms. The app is free to download and gives you a few free pages to try it. After that you need a subscription or pre-paid pages that never expire. All the audio you've created stays yours to listen to as much as you like, no subscription needed. Plans: I'm working on a web + API version and already have a small waiting list. What would you listen to first: textbooks, articles, or books in another language? I'll be here all day. Any feedback, bugs or ideas are very welcome!

text: It sounds like a cool idea, at least the way OpenAI presents it. However, going to the page and requirements, I have to nope out. I wish there was a reduced security mode that really just focuses on patching vulnerable software, and not defending itself from when the machine is already compromised as root. Because if your organization already has this bleeding-edge measured boot setup, then I believe quickly deploying a patch really is not a big deal anymore.

title: NariQ: BF16-level Qwen3.8-27B in a 10 GB file
text: We built NariQ: 3-bit-or-lower quantizations of Qwen3.8-27B that retain near-BF16 quality across agentic tasks, math, multilingual reasoning, and image understanding. To our knowledge, this is the first 3-bit-or-lower quantization that retains BF16 lvl performance on long-horizon agentic tasks. Benchmarks (BF16 / 3-bit / 2.5-bit / 2-bit): - DeepSWE: 39.8 / 41.0 / 41.9 / 28.6 - Terminal-Bench 2.1: 62.6 / 63.8 / 60.2 / 52.4 - AIME 25+26: 97.7 / 98.3 / 96.5 / 86.0 - MSGM: 94.0 / 93.1 / 91.8 / 90.6 - RealWorldQA: 82.4 / 82.4 / 81.3 / 80.9 Decode speed is comparable to other quants on an RTX PRO 6000. Context-length results below (3-bit / 2.5-bit / 2-bit / Unsloth UD-IQ3_XXS): - 4K: 88.9 / 99.2 / 111.7 / 94.7 - 16K: 84.5 / 93.8 / 105.1 / 89.8 - 64K: 70.7 / 77.5 / 85.0 / 74.8 Running these currently require our llama.cpp fork: ( https://github.com/nari-labs/nari-llama.cpp ) Feedback and questions welcome. title: Governor, Reserve Bank of India meets Chairpersons and Managing Directors & Chief Executive Officers of select UCBs and Industry Representatives in Mumbai on November 23, 2026
text: As part of the Reserve Bank of India's continued engagement with regulated entities, the Governor today met in Mumbai with the Chairpersons and Managing Directors & Chief Executive Officers (MDs & CEOs) of select Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) across different tiers. Representatives of the National Urban Cooperative Finance and Development Corporation Limited and the National Federation of Urban Co-operative Banks & Credit Societies Limited also participated. The meeting was also attended by Deputy Governors Shri Swaminathan J., Dr Poonam Gupta, Shri S. C. Murmu and Shri Rohit Jain, along with other senior officers of the Reserve Bank. In his opening remarks, the Governor noted that credit growth in the sector had improved, while growth in profitability had lagged. He emphasised the need to strengthen governance standards and support sustainable growth through prudent lending, with due regard to borrowers' repayment capacity. The Governor welcomed participants' positive feedback on Mission SAKSHAM, the Reserve Bank's ongoing training initiative for UCBs, and urged banks to make full use of it. As UCBs adopt technology, he advised them to put robust cybersecurity frameworks in place, underscoring that cyber risk affects banks of every size. He also emphasised the importance of customer centricity and of maintaining high standards in internal grievance redressal. Participants offered feedback and suggestions on policy and operational matters concerning the UCB sector. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1553

title: RBI releases 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs)
text: State Bank of India, HDFC Bank, and ICICI Bank continue to be identified as Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) under the same bucketing structure as in the 2025 list of D-SIBs . The additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) requirement for these D-SIBs will be in addition to the capital conservation buffer. The list of D-SIBs is as follows: Bucket Banks Additional Common Equity Tier 1 requirement as a percentage of Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs) 5 - 1% 4 State Bank of India 0.80% 3 - 0.60% 2 HDFC Bank 0.40% 1 ICICI Bank 0.20% Background: The Reserve Bank had issued the Framework for dealing with Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) on July 22, 2014 , which was subsequently updated on December 28, 2023 . The D-SIB framework requires the Reserve Bank to disclose the names of banks designated as D-SIBs starting from 2015 and place these banks in appropriate buckets depending upon their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs). Based on the bucket in which a D-SIB is placed, an additional common equity requirement has to be applied to it. In case a foreign bank having branch presence in India is a Global Systemically Important Bank (G-SIB) , it has to maintain additional CET1 capital surcharge in India as applicable to it as a G-SIB, proportionate to its Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs) in India, i.e., additional CET1 buffer prescribed by the home regulator (amount) multiplied by India RWA as per consolidated global Group books divided by total consolidated global Group RWA. The Reserve Bank had announced SBI and ICICI Bank as D-SIBs in 2015 and 2016 while HDFC Bank was classified as D-SIB in 2017 along with SBI and ICICI Bank. The current update is based on the data collected from banks as on March 31, 2026. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1547

title: Reserve Bank of India (All India Financial Institutions - Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026
text: RBI/2026-27/307 DOR.STR.REC.259/21-04-177/2026-27 November 23, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (All India Financial Institutions - Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026 Please refer to Reserve Bank of India (All India Financial Institutions - Securitisation Transactions) Directions, 2025 . 2. On a review, and in exercise of the powers conferred by the Section 45L of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, the Reserve Bank being satisfied that it is necessary and expedient in the public interest so to do, hereby issues the Amendment Directions hereinafter specified. 3. The Amendment Directions shall come into effect from April 01, 2027. 4. The Amendment Directions modify the Reserve Bank of India (All India Financial Institutions - Securitisation Transactions) Directions, 2025 as under: (1) Para 26 shall be substituted by the following, namely: “26. The issuance, holding and subsequent transfer of securitisation notes under these Directions shall only be in a dematerialised form. The minimum ticket size shall be ₹1 Crore at the time of issuance as well as at any subsequent transfers. The originator shall ensure that the agreement with the SPE requires the latter to put in place necessary arrangements with entities such as the registrar, depository, stock exchange etc., as may be applicable, to ensure compliance with the minimum ticket-size requirement. Provided that securitisation notes with amortisation structures shall be permitted to be traded at amortised value, if the ticket size falls below ₹1 crore. Explanation: Ticket size, for the purpose of these directions, refers to the size of investment by a single investor.” (2) Para 27 shall be substituted by the following, namely: “27. With respect to offer of securitisation notes to the public, Regulation 21 of SEBI (Issue and Listing of Securitised Debt Instruments and Security Receipts) Regulations, 2008, as amended from time to time, shall be complied with.” (3) Paragraph 27A shall be inserted as below: “27A. Transactions in securitisation notes issued prior to April 01, 2027, shall also be undertaken in compliance with the requirements mentioned in Paragraph 26 & 27 above.” (Vaibhav Chaturvedi) Chief General Manager
